note: The loop breaker's second branch, started 2026-11-28 00:15 after the first neurons' generation test (loop_breaker_rules.json's outcome) and before any run of this file. The first neurons (IF repeating AND at a line end THEN </think>) cut greedy loops on the 96 check prompts from 28 to 12 (17 fixed, 1 new, paired sign test 7e-5; 16 of the 17 left their text after the neurons fired; finished 60 -> 75; right 41 -> 42; KL 0.5778 -> 0.5815). What is left is the program's own gap: of the 35 answers whose thinking the neurons closed, 16 finished with no further firing, and in 15 the neurons fired again 120 to 620 tokens later, in the answer part, and wrote </think> a second time (13 of 15); 10 of those became loops of nothing but </think> lines, 5 ran to the cap. Read at those second firings (check prompts, so this is description, not a blind forecast): the answer was already stated in most, and 5 of the 15 would count as right if the answer ended there. The missing branch: IF repeating AND at a line end AND the thinking is closed THEN <|im_end|> (and no </think>).
first: loop_breaker_rules.json (the first neurons: breaker.pt, its probe w, constant c, line-end read n, threshold b, write v)
known_before_the_fit: From the first fit's captures (the unedited model's answers to the 160 fitting prompts; scratch scripts, 2026-11-28 00:05): (1) In the 104 finished answers the first neurons' gate never opens at a line end after the close (0 of 863 closed line ends, fitting and held out), so a second branch with the same gate would not touch ordinary answers. (2) In the 7 answers that loop after closing their thinking by themselves the gate opens at 743 closed line ends, 741 inside a verbatim repeat: the same probe detects answer-part loops. (3) The model's own logits do not say which stop token is due: where the gate opens, </think> minus <|im_end|> is 0.8 (median) with the thinking open and -0.4 with it closed, both about 10 logits under the top token; so raising both and letting the model choose does not work, and the branch needs its own read of 'the thinking is closed'. (4) That read, as a ridge readout from the last MLP's input fit on the first captures: AUROC 0.9997 on held-out positions, but loose as a number: open positions -0.30 to 0.62 (0.1% and max), closed positions 0.17 to 1.33 (median 0.83); at the first firing in the 5 held-out closed loops it read 0.3, 0.54, 0.98, 1.03, 1.08 (low where the answer part reads like thinking: 'Wait, let's check the question again'). Too loose to gate a threshold with (a gain of 20 would move the probe's threshold by +-5 against a typical margin of 3.5).

fit.what: The model with the first neurons in answers loop_breaker's 160 fitting prompts (same settings and seed). The unedited model, the neurons out, is then teacher-forced over those answers and captured as loop_breaker's fit captured its own (capture/, head.pt): the last MLP's input for the reads, the final residual and logits for the screen.
fit.why: The second branch acts after a forced close, and the first captures hold only 7 answers that loop after a close of their own. These answers give the read of 'closed' its hard cases (thinking-like text after a close) and the screen its loops.

design.written: 2026-11-28 00:25, before the fit stage ran (it is queued) and before any generation with a second pair. From the first captures alone (unedited answers to the fitting prompts), so it may be amended once the fit stage's answers are in; any amendment is recorded below with its reason.
design.neurons: Four. The first pair is loop_breaker's, weight for weight. The second pair: gate k (w.x - b c.x - line (c.x - n.x)), the first pair's gate with the line-end read moved into it (repeating AND at a line end; the clamp pair as before), up projection m.x (the closed read), write dose * v_end - v, where v is the first pair's write (</think> +16, <|im_end|> +2.1) and v_end the unit write that raises <|im_end|> by 1 and </think> by 0. So where the first pair fires at a line end the four together write about (1 - m.x) of v and m.x * dose of v_end: </think> while the read says open, <|im_end|> when it says closed, a mix in between.
design.why_this_form: A SwiGLU neuron is one threshold times one linear read. 'Repeating' needs the threshold; 'at a line end' reads cleanly enough (0.76 to 1.04 at line ends, at most 0.25 elsewhere) to share the gate; the closed read does not (see known_before_the_fit), so it takes the linear place, where its error scales a write instead of moving a threshold. Reading the hard cases: with m.x about 0.3 the pair still writes most of </think> (a second close, as the first pair alone does now) and the next line end, behind two closes, reads closed. Three thresholds would need a second layer (a register written by a neuron in layer 30); not tried.

closed.read: m: the ridge least-squares read of 'a </think> is among the tokens before this position' (1 or 0) from the last MLP's input, on the fitting prompts' answers of both sets (the unedited model's and the first pair's), every position up to a second </think>.

design.split: By prompt, loop_breaker's own split of the fitting prompts (the prompts its probe, constant and line-end read were fit on), for both sets of answers.

screen.how: Teacher-forced, from the captured final residuals, over the unedited top five tokens and the two stop tokens, as loop_breaker's. On the unedited model's answers: where the four first change the unedited argmax, against where the first pair alone does. On the first pair's answers: where the four's argmax first differs from the first pair's.
screen.populations: think: unedited answers whose first change by the first pair alone is </think> with the thinking open (outcome 'kept' if the four make the same first change). closed: answers of either set where the first pair fires (activation above 0.5) after a close and before any second </think> (outcome 'ended' if the four first differ with <|im_end|> at a closed position). done: the other finished answers ('none' if unchanged). An <|im_end|> while the thinking is open is 'end_in_think' anywhere.
screen.allowed: On the fitting prompts a dose is allowed with no end_in_think, at most max(1, 2%) of the done answers changed and at least 90% of the think answers kept.
screen.select: Of the allowed doses the smallest that ends the most closed answers, then the next dose of the grid if allowed too: a step of margin, because the closed read is lowest in the hard cases and the preview on the first captures showed no harm at any dose up to 40.
screen.gate: Generation runs only if, on the held-out prompts, the selected dose ends at least 60% of the closed answers, with no end_in_think, at most 5% of the done answers changed and at least 90% of the think answers kept.

design.preview: First captures only, closed read fit on them alone (scratch, 2026-11-28 00:20): at every dose from 12 to 40, 105 of 105 other finished answers unchanged and no <|im_end|> inside the thinking; the first pair's closes kept in 23 of 23 fitting and 18 of 20 held-out answers (the other 2 close at another line end); the 7 answers that loop after their own close end with <|im_end|> from dose 24 on (held out: 2 of 5 at dose 12, 4 at 16 and 20, 5 from 24).

fresh.why: The check prompts (GSM8K test rows 16-111) were read to design this branch, so they cannot test it blind. GSM8K test rows 112-207, never generated on before, are the blind test: unedited and the final neurons, greedy, 2,048 new tokens, the check's settings. The check prompts are run as well, for the comparison with every earlier number, and reported as not blind.

generate.settings: As loop_breaker's test: greedy, 2,048 new tokens, fp32 state, seed 26103102, the full vocabulary.
generate.check: The 96 check prompts with the four neurons (arm breaker2), against the unedited model (28 loops, 60 finished, 41 right) and the first pair (12, 75, 42) on the same build. Not blind: these prompts' answers under the first pair shaped the design.
generate.fresh: GSM8K test rows 112-207: unedited and breaker2, then the first pair alone (arm breaker) to say blind what the second pair adds.

predictions.closed_read: Fit on both sets, at held-out positions where the first pair fires: closed median at least 0.6 and 10% quantile at least 0.4; open 99% quantile at most 0.3. Confidence 60%: the first captures gave closed 0.44 to 0.78 per-loop medians and open 0.23, and the new answers add the hard cases to the fit.
predictions.check: Not blind. Loops 5 or fewer (first pair 12, unedited 28); finished at least 85 (75, 60); right at least 44 (42, 41: at the 15 second firings 5 answers would count as right if they ended there); no answer with three or more </think> tokens (first pair: 11); KL within 0.006 of unedited (first pair +0.0037). Confidence 55% for the loops.
predictions.fresh: Blind. With U the unedited model's loops on the fresh prompts (expected 20 to 32): the four neurons leave at most U/4 (one-sided paired sign test under 0.001), finish at least 15 more answers, change right by -2 or better, and leave no answer with three or more </think> tokens; the first pair alone leaves between the two. Confidence 55%.
predictions.fail: Ways it fails: the closed read is too low in answer parts that read like thinking, so the second close stays (graceful: the next line end ends it); <|im_end|> inside the thinking where the read is high by error (the answer ends with no answer); the answer part repeats the thinking's text before it reaches its final line and is ended early (a finished answer without an answer).

criteria: The claim 'the two branches fix the greedy loops' needs, on the fresh prompts, the paired sign test under 0.05 against unedited and no rise in answers that end without closing their thinking; the claim 'the second branch adds to the first' needs fewer loops than the first pair alone on the fresh prompts (paired sign test under 0.05).

Whether the repeat probe fires on these short restatements is not known (no captures of sampled answers).
sampled.predictions: The first pair fires (above 0.5) in 15 to 35 answers and the second in at most 8; finished rises by 5 to 20; right and finished changes by -2 to +6; no finished answer without a </think>; of the 59 answers the unedited model finished sampled, at least 50 are token-identical. Confidence 50%: the probe was fit on greedy loops, and a +16 logit write decides a sampled token as surely as a greedy one.
sampled.criteria: 'No harm sampled': right and finished falls by at most 3 and no rise in answers that end without closing their thinking. 'Helps sampled': more answers newly finished than newly unfinished by a paired one-sided sign test under 0.05. A changed answer's continuation is resampled, so single right/wrong flips are noise; totals and the sign tests are what count.
